expectedFacts: The alpha handling the write asks Zero's ShouldServe to serve the field, proposing its OWN group id as the requested owner.
Zero records the assignment by proposing it through its Raft group; if another group already owns it, the first assignment wins and the existing owner is returned.
Reserved internal predicates are forced onto group 1 by Zero's ShouldServe regardless of which group asked (so that ACL updates stream from one group and restore after a drop-all is simpler).

When the identifier map has no direct Zero connection (the live loader builds it with only a client connection to an alpha), its background refill goroutine calls the alpha's AllocateUIDs API for blocks of 100,000 IDs.
On the alpha, the allocate-IDs RPC first calls AuthorizeCapability with the lease-UIDs capability, then worker.AssignUidsOverNetwork.
That function goes through the active ZeroHooks; the default implementation forwards the request (with the incoming metadata) to the Zero leader's AssignIds.

A gRPC identity interceptor (documented to be installed ahead of the audit interceptor) calls WithResolvedIdentity, which runs the installed or built-in Authenticator and attaches the resulting Principal to the request context; it never rejects the request.
The built-in ACL authenticator parses the ACL JWT, requires an exp claim, and builds a Principal with subject, groups, claims and method 'acl'.

edgraph.extractUserAndGroups first tries userDataFromPrincipal, which rebuilds user data from the Principal when Method is acl and the namespace claim is present; otherwise it falls back to parsing the JWT.
The update is forwarded to the group-1 leader, which stores the schema text as a value of a reserved predicate on a single schema node and commits it.

Each alpha's admin server starts a background SubscribeForUpdates on that schema predicate's key prefix for group 1; it connects to a group-1 member and receives the updated posting list over a Subscribe stream.

The subscriber callback skips stale versions or unchanged text, regenerates the GraphQL schema, and swaps it in (resetSchema) only if the namespace's schema was already loaded; otherwise it is lazy-loaded later.

r3-dgraph-15.query: If I want an AI assistant to explore data through the tool endpoint that the database server process itself exposes (not a separately started helper), but never change anything, what is provided for that and what exactly keeps it from writing?

expectedFacts: Not implemented: NewUriHandler handles only file (or empty) and minio/s3 schemes; any other scheme returns 'Unable to handle url'.
The same two remote schemes (minio, s3) are all filestore and x.MinioClient recognise; the only mention of azure:// is a comment about how a new scheme handler would be added.
Other object stores can be reached only if they speak the S3 API, through the minio:// or s3:// scheme with a custom host; there is no native GCS or Azure client.
Not implemented: the full-text functions (alloftext, anyoftext) return boolean matches; allof* is an intersection and anyof* a union of index posting lists, returned in UID order.
Users can only reorder with orderasc/orderdesc on a field; no term-frequency or scoring data is stored in the index.
The only scored ranking is vector similarity search (similar_to over HNSW vector indexes), which ranks by vector distance, not by text relevance.
